client.name: Eric Millington · Pixelheap
client.tagline: Senior brand & web design, Clifton Park, NY

summary: The work is the strongest thing here: 25 years of brand, web and print for organizations like GlobalFoundries, SPAC and the Freihofer's Saratoga Jazz Festival, on a fast, well-built site with good accessibility basics. The problem is that almost nobody can find it. In our search snapshot, neither your name nor your studio surfaced, and your site describes you three different ways. Fix the name, the story and the signals, and the score moves quickly.

pillars.name: Discoverability
pillars.notes: None of 5 searches surfaced pixelheap.design or you. Namesakes (Ernest, Errol, Elliot Millington) own your name. Your name isn't in the home page title.

pillars.name: Consistency
pillars.notes: Three different positioning statements on one site (art director / studio / front-end developer), 20+ vs 25+ years, I vs we.

pillars.name: Ownership & Control
pillars.notes: You own the domain and a self-hosted site. Only one profile (LinkedIn) is linked; no Behance/Dribbble/Google Business Profile found. Registrar, 2FA and email setup still to confirm.

pillars.name: Privacy & Safety
pillars.notes: No home address found. Personal cell published on every page, quote form requires a phone number, Google tag loads with no consent notice. Data broker sweep and breach check not yet run.

pillars.name: Reputation & Content
pillars.notes: Excellent, recognizable client list and a personable blog. No testimonials or reviews visible; blog quiet since Nov 2025.

pillars.name: Website Quality
pillars.notes: HTTPS, lang, viewport, alt text on all 18 images, one H1, social preview tags, sitemap. But no security headers, 21 scripts incl. two form plugins on the home page, and a tracker.

findings.title: Searchers can't find you by name or by studio
findings.detail: Across 5 searches (your name, name + designer, name + town, 'Pixelheap' + service + town, and the domain itself), none returned your site or a profile of yours. Results were namesakes, unrelated 'pixel' studios and local competitors. Note: this snapshot used one search engine; we'll confirm in signed-out Google from your area.

findings.title: Your name isn't in the home page title
findings.detail: The title reads 'Senior Designer - Pixelheap.Design - Brand & Web Design - Clifton Park, NY' (74 characters, so it gets truncated). The H1 is 'Eric Millington', but the title is what search engines weigh. Suggested title: 'Eric Millington · Brand & Web Designer, Clifton Park NY | Pixelheap'.

findings.title: Three different stories about who you are
findings.detail: The home page says 'a design studio led by a senior art director'. The portfolio says 'I'm a front-end developer with a background in print design'. The quote page mixes 'I' and 'us'. A prospect reading two pages gets two people. Pick one positioning and one voice, then write a canonical bio (short/medium/long) and reuse it everywhere.

findings.title: '20+ years' and '25+ years' on the same page
findings.detail: The hero says 20+ years and the About section says 25+. Both are true-ish; only one should appear.
findings.evidence: Home page hero vs. 'About Eric Millington'

findings.title: Phone number on every page; the quote form requires one
findings.detail: 'Call or text: 518.229.3364' appears in the content and footer site-wide, so scrapers will harvest it. If it's your personal cell, use a business line (Google Voice, OpenPhone). The quote form also makes phone number required; making it optional reduces friction and collects less data.

findings.title: Google tag loads with no consent notice
findings.detail: Site Kit injects Google's gtag (GT-PJ43BXS) on every page. For a US studio this is common, but it conflicts with the privacy-first story you'll be selling. Use cookieless analytics (Plausible or Fathom), or add a proper consent banner.

findings.title: Unclaimed profiles where clients look
findings.detail: No Google Business Profile, Behance, Dribbble or chamber listing was found. Local competitors (3tone Digital, Clever Coding) rank through exactly these. 'Heapix.design' already exists on Dribbble, so reserve 'pixelheap' on major platforms now.

findings.title: Two form plugins and 21 scripts on the home page
findings.detail: Contact Form 7 and WPForms both load, including WPForms' address field, input-mask and country list, on a page with no form. Load forms only on the quote page and remove the unused plugin.

findings.title: No security headers
findings.detail: HSTS, Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are all missing. That's a few lines in .htaccess on Apache.

findings.title: Great client list, no social proof
findings.detail: GlobalFoundries, SPAC and the Freihofer's Jazz Festival are a strong list, but there are no testimonials, no reviews and no results ('traffic up X%'). Ask 3 past clients for two sentences each.

findings.title: Blog quiet for nearly a year
findings.detail: The last post was Nov 23, 2025. The voice is great ('Build your website for a doom-scrolling goldfish'). Even one post a month on topics clients search for would help discoverability.

findings.title: Small hygiene items
findings.detail: Headings skip from H2 to H4. The LinkedIn link is written 'Https://'. The quote page has no meta description. An auto-titled page (/1739-2/) is still published.

now.title: Fix the home page title
now.detail: Use 'Eric Millington · Brand & Web Designer, Clifton Park NY | Pixelheap' and add meta descriptions to the quote and blog pages.

now.title: Reserve 'pixelheap' everywhere
now.detail: Behance, Dribbble, Instagram, Bluesky, Threads, YouTube. Even if you don't post yet.

now.title: Claim Google Business Profile
now.detail: As a service-area business, so your address stays hidden. Category: Graphic designer / Website designer.

now.title: Decide on the phone number
now.detail: Get a business line if it's your personal cell, and make phone optional on the quote form.

next.title: One positioning, one voice
next.detail: Write the canonical bio (short/medium/long) and apply it to every page, LinkedIn and every new profile.

next.title: Add three testimonials
next.detail: Ask past clients (SPAC, Troy Cabinet, Saratoga Wine & Food). Put them on home and portfolio.

next.title: Lighten and harden the site
next.detail: Remove the unused form plugin, load forms only on the quote page, add security headers, switch to cookieless analytics.

next.title: Privacy sweep
next.detail: Check data brokers for your name and home address, run a breach check on your business emails, enable 2FA on the registrar and WordPress admin.

later.title: Publish a monthly post
later.detail: Pick topics clients search for, e.g. 'What a website redesign costs in the Capital Region' or 'Signs your site needs a design rescue'.

later.title: Local directory listings
later.detail: Capital Region Chamber, Clutch, BBB, with consistent name, URL and bio.

later.title: Re-audit in 90 days
later.detail: Target: Presence Score 75+, owning the top 3 results for your name.
